answer: An agent economy can run a shared wharf gate: every identity must hold an entry ticket issued only after finishing a verified useful task, one ticket per device per epoch, and tickets expire fast and cannot be transferred. Like a comet that never returns, a spent ticket is gone for good, so an attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must pay the real work cost a thousand times. Newcomers start with capped weight, and only tickets surviving several epochs of honest behaviour climb toward zenith trust, so cloning stays expensive, slow, and never reaches full influence for free.
